method: Independent check of a 10-item stratified sample. SEC items read from the filing index, primary 8-K and exhibits (99.1, 99.2, 10.1) and the EDGAR submission header for the filing date. Web items read with one fetch each; The Real Deal returned HTTP 403, so its existence and core facts were confirmed by two ordinary web searches only. Titles were re-read from articles.json at 11:33 local because the SEC-item titles were rewritten during the check; the rewritten titles are the ones judged.

sample.title: Dream Finders 8-K: closes $2.2B Beazer purchase with $572M Millrose land-bank facility

facts.claim: Closed the all-cash Beazer purchase Oct. 20, 2026
facts.source_says: 8-K Item 2.01: completed Oct. 20, 2026; ex. 99.1: all-cash transaction
$33.50 in cash per Beazer share
ex. 99.1: enterprise value of approximately $2.2 billion
ex. 99.1: nation's sixth-largest homebuilder (by CY2025 revenue)

aggregate proceeds of $572.1 million from the land bank facility committed by Millrose (incl. Kennedy Lewis affiliates), used to redeem Beazer's $350M 7.250% 2029 notes and repay Beazer's credit facility
Not in the Dream Finders filing; Millrose's Oct. 27 ex. 99.1 says approximately 7,000 homesites
$225.0M Series B convertible preferred on Sept. 14 + $450.0M at closing = $675M. The 12% dividend is stated only in Millrose's ex. 99.1, not in this filing

facts.claim: About $488M of the preferred is Millrose's
facts.source_says: Millrose ex. 99.1: approximately $488M (net of original issue discount): $171M on Sept. 14 and $317M at closing. Not in this filing
The aggregate consideration paid in connection with the Merger was approximately $878.4 million

sample.score_comment: floor85-competitor-deal (Millrose deal with a named builder) and floor75-builder-ma (ranks 14 and 21) both apply; 93 is in the right band for a competitor whole-company financing of a top-25 builder merger.
fixes_needed: Optional precision: in the summary and the suggested_update, write 'about $488M (net of original issue discount)' and cite Millrose's Oct. 27 release for the 12% rate, 7,000 homesites and $488M, because the linked Dream Finders filing does not state them.

facts.claim: Millrose bought 1,233 completed Lennar homes in 18 states for about $333M as rentals, disclosed with Q3 results
facts.source_says: Page blocked (HTTP 403); search snippet of the article and Millrose's Oct. 27 ex. 99.1 both give 1,233 homes, 18 states, about $333M cost basis ($120M of balance-sheet capital + $213M of limited-recourse financing)

Securities class action by Leon and Sylvia Rubenstein against Millrose, its CEO and its CFO (filed Oct. 9) alleges Millrose bought Lennar homes and rented them at a loss. It names Millrose, not Lennar, and was filed before this Q3 disclosure

fixes_needed: Reword the Hunterbrook sentence to what is supported, e.g. 'Lennar stock fell Oct. 2 after Hunterbrook Media, whose affiliate is short Lennar and Millrose, reported Millrose had been buying Lennar homes and renting them at a loss.' Drop 'late-quarter sales ... helped it hit targets' unless a source is found.

sample.title: LGI Homes 8-K: amends revolver to about $1.166B, $855M extended to Oct 2030

facts.claim: Amended its revolver on Oct. 9, 2026; Wells Fargo is agent
facts.source_says: Seventh Amendment dated Oct. 9, 2026; Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. as administrative agent (filed Oct. 14)

facts.claim: Commitments total about $1.166B including a $175M incremental facility
facts.source_says: Commitments are $1,165,982,142.85 (cut from $1,182,500,000). The $175M is an uncommitted accordion on top: Section 2.17 lets commitments rise by up to $175M (up from $95M), capped at $1.3B in total. It is not part of the $1.166B

facts.claim: Borrowing-base values and covenants modified; details not disclosed
facts.source_says: modified borrowing base values and certain financial and other covenants (details are in ex. 10.1, not the 8-K body)

facts.claim: why_it_matters: LGI owns most of its land and funds it on this revolver
facts.source_says: The 8-K gives no owned/optioned lot mix

sample.score_comment: floor70-financing (amended credit facility, rank 20). 70 is right. The commitment cut from $1.1825B to $1.166B is the more relevant detail for a land banker and is missing.
fixes_needed: Summary: replace 'commitments total about $1.166B including a $175M incremental facility' with 'commitments about $1.166B (down from $1.1825B), plus an accordion of up to $175M (up from $95M) capped at $1.3B'.
suggested_update text: same correction ('commitments about $1.166B, down from $1.1825B; accordion up to $175M, capped at $1.3B; $855M (73.3%) now matures 2030-10-09').
why_it_matters: support 'owns most of its land' from LGI's 10-Q lot table, or soften it.

sample.score_comment: In substance 24 (noise) is the right call, but it contradicts the rubric as written: floor75-competitor covers 'any Millrose filing, release or earnings call', and the routine-filing cap (45) lists only 10-Q/10-K cover entries, earnings-date 8-Ks, shareholder votes and bylaw changes, not dividend declarations. Nothing in the rubric lets this item score 24. Scored under v1.1.
fixes_needed: Preferred: rubric v1.4 adds dividend declarations to the routine-filing cap and says the routine cap beats floor75-competitor; then 24 stands and the item records that cap. Otherwise the floor forces 75. Also add 'an increase' to the summary ('...$0.79 per share, an increase, payable...').

summary.notes: Failed: ef17c22b721c (21, not 22, counterparties outside Lennar), 6b383809f6a9 (the $175M is an accordion on top of the $1.166B, which itself was cut from $1.1825B), 47d817b59696 (score 24 contradicts floor75-competitor as written; fix the rubric rather than the score). Every link, title, date and publisher checked out; all 6 SEC filing dates match the EDGAR 'filed as of' date. The Real Deal page is blocked (403), so c5a94aef0506 was checked only through search snippets, and its Hunterbrook 'late-quarter sales to hit targets' claim could not be verified; reword it before the CEO sees it. Pattern: summaries pull facts from related filings (Dream Finders' item uses the 12%/7,000/$488M figures from Millrose's release) and why_it_matters adds unsourced judgments ('leverage above its own target', 'owns most of its land'). Neither is wrong yet, but each should cite or be softened. SEC-item titles were rewritten in articles.json during this check; the new titles are accurate.
